description: Assertions for tools/prose-eval.js. Per-rule, not per-file: a fixture says nothing about rules it does not name.

cases.why: serves as / stands as / boasts, all in the copula-dodging sense.
testament to / underscores the importance / plays a crucial role / marks a pivotal moment.
highlighting / underscoring / showcasing tails that interpret rather than report.
data tells us / numbers speak for themselves / conclusion emerges.
Four authority claims, no citation anywhere in the file.
Same, in LaTeX. Guards the case where stripLatex substitution suppresses the rule outright: \ref is present but no \cite.
Every authority claim carries \cite / \citep / \citet / \citeauthor. Regression guard for the [CITE] substitution in stripLatex.
Same claims in markdown across all three citation forms: [@key], [14], (Kim et al., 2014).
demonstrating / illustrating / reflecting tails report results; 'the results suggest' and 'the findings indicate' are standard hedging, not actorless claims.
serves (with object), observers, reserve, servers, stood as, standard, outstanding. Word-boundary regression guard.
Citation lands two sentences later, inside the 200-character tolerance. Suppression is deliberate: a missing citation three sentences out is a copyedit pass, not a rigor failure.

Both kinds exceed max_count, and both must fire on .tex. Regression guard for the native repeated-phrase engine: before it existed these rules ran only through the optional Python pass, which is skipped for LaTeX, so the error-severity slogan rule never ran on a paper draft.
Two 'What X ... is Y' clefts inside 220 chars. Regression guard for the native proximity engine, same .tex gap.
One 'load-bearing' (max_count 1) and two 'structurally' (max_count 2). At the allowance, not over it. Guards the off-by-one.

scotopic / photopic / linear / saturation / supra-threshold / ballistic regime are neutral domain vocabulary. Guards the suppress_pattern port from muriel.aiism RULE_SUPPRESS, which native previously lacked entirely on .tex.
